title: Roulette
subtitle: Betting Systems Analysis
overview: A game of pure chance where players bet on where a ball will land on a spinning wheel. Used here to demonstrate why all betting systems fail.
rules: House edge is built into the wheel itself

algorithm.name: Monte Carlo Analysis
algorithm.description: We simulate thousands of sessions using different betting systems to prove they all converge to the same negative expected value.

proof.explanation: The house edge is mathematically identical for ALL bet types in American roulette.
proof.formula: E[Profit] = P(win) x payout + P(lose) x (-1) = -2/38 = -5.26%
steps: Green pockets create the house edge
Payouts assume 36 pockets, but there are 38
proof.conclusion: The house edge cannot be avoided. Every bet loses 5.26 cents per dollar on average.

proof.explanation: The probability appears close to 50%, but green pockets make all the difference.
steps: 18 red numbers out of 38 total pockets
proof.conclusion: The 2.63% probability disadvantage creates the 5.26% house edge.

proof.explanation: The Optional Stopping Theorem proves no betting strategy can overcome negative expected value.
steps: Let X_t = cumulative profit at time t
Each bet has E[profit] = -5.26% x bet size
X_t is a supermartingale (expected value decreases)
For ANY stopping rule tau: E[X_tau] <= 0
proof.conclusion: Martingale, Fibonacci, 'quit while ahead' - ALL fail mathematically.

keyInsight: No betting system can overcome the house edge. Mathematics guarantees the house wins.
